placements.why: The deployment gate decision — requiring signed release manifests for Meridian deploys across staging and production — is an architectural decision about the deployment pipeline's security structure, establishing a strata category for pipeline and infrastructure decisions that future envelopes can nest under.
placements.title: deployment pipeline and infrastructure decisions
placements.frame: What architectural decisions shape the system's deployment, infrastructure, and pipeline structure?

placements.title: from unsigned artifacts reaching staging to mandatory signed manifests before any Meridian deploy
placements.frame: What binding preconditions does the organization impose on its deployment pipeline before artifacts ship, and what prior failures motivated them?
placements.why: All segments contribute to the theme of enforcing signed release manifests as a deployment gate for the Meridian release train: the directive itself (src-2), its reported version through Xena's voice (src-1), the incident justification citing two unsigned artifacts reaching staging (src-3), the ratifying 'Key decisions' header (src-4), and the summary fragments for gate, scope, and ownership (src-5, src-6, src-7). The incident in src-3 is a fact evidencing the gate theme, not a separate leaf.
